Preshpal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 6 January, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Jbp:653
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
At Jabalpur

Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pramod Kumar Agrawal
On The 6 th Of January, 2026
Misc .
Criminal Case No. 33914 of 2025

Preshpal
 Versus
 The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others
 Appearance:
 Ms. Saritha Achary - Advocate for applicant.
 Shri Yogesh Dhande - Government Advocate for State.

Order 
This is the fourth bail application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of BNSS for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.191/2023 registered at Police Station - Amarkantak, District Anuppur (M.P.) for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366-A, 368, 342, 376(2)(n), 506 of IPC and Sections 3(4)/5(6) of POCSO Act.
Applicant is in detention since 13.12.2024.
His third bail application was dismissed on merits on 04.07.2025.

2. As per the prosecution story, the allegation against the applicant is that he has taken away the minor prosecutrix with him and committed rape upon her therefore, the aforesaid offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant is innocent.
He is in custody since 13.12.2024.

It is further submitted that DNA report is NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:653 2 MCRC-33914-2025 doubtful.
It is further submitted that there was dispute with Kewat Prasad (PW-7), due to which applicant has been falsely implicated in this case.
There is omissions and contradictions in the statements of witnesses.
Charge sheet has been filed and trial will take considerable time.
Therefore, it has been prayed that the applicant may be released on bail.

4. On the other hand, learned counsel for State has opposed the grant of bail to the applicant and submitted that prosecutrix is minor and she has deposed against the present applicant in her Court statement.
DNA report is also positive.
His third bail application was dismissed on merits on 04.07.2025 in M.Cr.C. No.16583/2025 by passing a detailed order.
Thereafter, there is no material change in the circumstances.
It is further submitted that at this stage, minute appreciation of evidence cannot be done.
